recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed unless a future THO release removes COPYMark from the SecurityPolicy/PrivacyMark hierarchy or changes the SecurityControlObservationValue inclusion chain.
issue_request: FHIR-19311 was a Published FHIR-core Security change request with a Persuasive with Modification resolution. It began as a proposed integrity label for copied or duplicated data, but the accepted resolution was to include v3 ActCode PrivacyMark codes in the SecurityPolicy value set so copy/CUI-style marks could be used when appropriate.
initial_application: Jira records that Grahame updated the terminology server with current v3 MIF content on 2019-10-08 so CUI and CopyMark were present and flowed into HCS through SecurityControlObservationValue to v3-SecurityPolicy. Core history has no FHIR-19311-specific commit, but f04f624 updated source/v3/source.xml on that date, and 5c0494 later moved UTG/v3 content out of core while preserving the external THO value-set include.
additional_context: Current core source defines All Security Labels by including THO v3-SecurityControlObservationValue. THO defines that value set as including v3-SecurityPolicy, and ActCode currently contains SecurityPolicy > PrivacyMark > SecurityLabelMark > COPYMark. UP-128 is a later implemented UTG proposal in the same SecurityLabelMark family and confirms COPYMark as an existing sibling privacy-mark code.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Adding a duplicate core-local include or restating the THO hierarchy in core narrative would be redundant and could drift from the authoritative terminology source.

related_jiras.note: Later implemented UTG proposal under SecurityLabelMark; comments describe COPYMark as an existing sibling PrivacyMark code and confirm the terminology belongs in THO.
